bib.title: Improving Retrieval-Augmented Generation through Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Improving Retrieval-Augmented Generation through Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning" (MMOA-RAG). Yiqun Chen, Lingyong Yan, Weiwei Sun, Xinyu Ma, Yi Zhang, Shuaiqiang Wang, Dawei Yin, Yiming Yang, Jiaxin Mao (Renmin Univ., Baidu, CMU). NeurIPS 2025 (39th Conference). arXiv:2501.15228v2, 7 Oct 2025. Code: github.com/chenyiqun/MMOA-RAG.

COVERAGE: All 25 pages; 88,769 of 88,769 chars read (main text, references skimmed, Appendices A-I incl. Tables 6-8, pseudocode, case study). No NeurIPS checklist text appeared in the extraction. The figure-bar numbers in Fig 2 were read from extracted plot labels, not images.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- claim: Jointly training query rewriter, selector and generator with multi-agent PPO (MAPPO) on one shared F1 reward beats all re-implemented baselines on all 9 metrics (Contriever).
  number: HotpotQA F1 48.29 vs best baseline 46.49 (+1.80); 2Wiki F1 46.40 (+1.89); AmbigQA F1 48.59 (+2.67)
  setup: Llama-3-8B-Instruct for all methods, Contriever retriever, K=10 docs to selector, Wikipedia passages, no gold supporting passages used. Baselines re-implemented by authors.
  quote: "MMOA-RAG (ours)39.15 36.15 48.29 42.73 41.52 46.40 38.85 34.75 48.59 ... ∆+1.12 +1.55 +1.80 +1.71 +1.79 +1.89 +2.60 +2.20 +2.67"
  where: Table 1, p.7
- claim: Joint MAPPO training adds about 2-4 points over the same modules after SFT warm start alone, for three pipeline shapes.
  number: QR+S+G gains HotpotQA F1 +3.60 (44.69 to 48.29); S+G +3.93; QR+G +2.94; AmbigQA gains +1.37 to +2.22 F1
  setup: same as above; SFT = warm start, MAPPO = joint training on top
  quote: "the performance gains from MAPPO over SFT are approximately three percentage points on multi-hop datasets such as HotpotQA and 2WikiMultihopQA, while improvements on the single-hop dataset AmbigQA are around two percentage points."
  where: Table 2 and Sec 4.4, pp.8-9
- claim: Dropping any one agent from joint optimization lowers results; the full system is best. Leaving out the selector hurts least; leaving out the generator hurts most on single-hop AmbigQA. Authors say joint training gives the generator some denoising ability.
  number: HotpotQA F1 (plot labels, order as printed): w/o G 46.9, w/o S 47.6, w/o QR 46.0, full 48.3 (assignment of labels to series inferred from legend order)
  setup: ablation Fig 2; Fig 3 shows reward curve on AmbigQA converging fastest and highest for the full system
  quote: "the MMOA-RAG w/o S variant achieves the best performance among the three ablation configurations ... through the joint optimization by MAPPO, the Generator acquires some denoising capabilities."
  where: Sec 4.3, Fig 2/3, p.8
- claim: Untrained Llama-3-8B-Instruct gets no benefit from retrieved documents with Contriever; SFT on RAG format is what makes it use them.
  number: HotpotQA F1 31.18 (no RAG) vs 30.67 (vanilla RAG, no training) vs 44.49 (RAG with SFT)
  setup: Table 1, Contriever, Llama-3-8B-Instruct
  quote: "Vanilla RAG w/o train achieves comparable results to LLM w/o RAG across various metrics."
  where: Table 1, Sec 4.2, p.7
- claim: With stronger retrievers the margin shrinks and is sometimes negative; MMOA-RAG "surpasses most" baselines, not all.
  number: BGE: 2Wiki EM -0.10, HotpotQA F1 +0.68; E5: AmbigQA Acc -0.05, 2Wiki EM -0.06; best E5 gains HotpotQA F1 +1.38
  setup: Models trained with Contriever, then tested on BGE and E5 retrievers
  quote: "∆+0.56 +0.72 +0.68 +0.11-0.10+0.32 +0.15 +0.50 +0.39" (BGE) and "∆+0.80 +0.95 +1.38 +0.05-0.06+0.38-0.05+0.70 +1.05" (E5)
  where: Table 7, p.20
- claim: Out-of-domain (train HotpotQA, test AmbigQA) it still leads, narrowly; RetRobust is the strongest baseline there.
  number: F1 45.62 vs RetRobust 44.08 vs Rewrite-Retrieve-Read 43.61
  quote: "MMOA-RAG (ours)35.45 32.43 45.62"
  where: Table 8, p.20
- claim: Reward and penalty design: reward = F1 of final answer; small per-agent format penalties.
  number: rewriter -0.5 if more than four sub-questions; selector -1 for duplicate or malformed IDs; generator -0.5 for overlong answer
  quote: "PQR is assigned a value of -0.5 if the number of sub-questions exceeds four" ; "P S is set to -1"; "When the generated answer exceeds a certain length, PG is set to -0.5"
  where: Sec 3.3, pp.4-5
- claim: Training cost grows linearly with agents; inference cost is unchanged.
  number: none (n times the rollout/update time for n agents)
  quote: "When we have n agents, the time required for rollouts and updating model parameters becomes n times that of a single agent." / "Training with multiple agents does not introduce any additional overhead during the inference phase."
  where: App G, p.21
- claim: Selector SFT labels are made cheaply by word overlap with question+gold answer (no GPT-4o labelling; BGM's Synthesis SPS judged costly). Selector action space is restricted to document-ID tokens to cut exploration.
  number: none
  quote: "if any word from Setqi appears in Setdi,j , the ID of corresponding document j is included in the final output as the Label of SFT."
  where: App B.2, p.16; Eq 5
- claim: Candidate pool is fixed at K=10 whatever the number of sub-questions (e.g. 2 sub-questions give top-5 each). Retriever is frozen, treated as environment.
  number: K=10
  quote: "if the Query Rewriter yields 2 sub-questions, each sub-question is used for retrieval, with the top-5 documents from each retrieval being selected"
  where: App D.2, p.19
- Hyperparameters (Table 6, p.19): beta 0.06-0.2 (KL to SFT model), gamma 1.0, lambda 0.95, clip 0.2, critic coef alpha 0.1, max lr 2e-5, buffer 128, cosine schedule, top_p 0.9. Built on LLaMA-Factory PPO code.
- Case study (App I): after MAPPO the rewriter splits the Vermont question into 2 sub-questions, the selector picks one document and the answer is correct ("North Atlantic Conference"). The SFT-only system uses 1 sub-question, selects 8 of 10 docs and answers "Yankee Conference" (wrong).

LIMITS
- Concedes: retriever not optimized (frozen Contriever, dense); only 3 trainable agents; parameter sharing "can lead to instability when the number of agents increases" (not tested beyond 3).
- Future work stated: DAG pipelines, dynamic agentic RAG workflows, reward balancing effectiveness against cost and latency; reward is F1 only, no cost term.
- Not shown: only Llama-3-8B-Instruct; QA only (HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA, AmbigQA), Wikipedia corpus; no variance or seeds reported; gains of ~1-2.7 points over re-implemented baselines; gains vanish or reverse on some metrics with BGE/E5; the paper gives no comparison with Search-r1 / R1-Searcher in tables (only mentioned in related work); no dataset sizes or training-sample counts in main text beyond Fig 3 axis (up to ~60k samples).
- Dated: 2023-24 baselines (Self-RAG, BGM, RAG-DDR); agentic-search RL work has since moved on.

BUILDS ON
MAPPO (Yu et al. [53], StarCraft II setting); PPO (Schulman et al. [38]); GAE [37]; InstructGPT-style KL-to-SFT reward [31]; Rewrite-Retrieve-Read [29] (also source of rewriter SFT data); BGM [22] (bridge/selector idea); RAG-DDR [27]; RetRobust [52]; Self-RAG [1]; Contriever [16]; RAG original (Lewis et al. [25]); end-to-end RAG work REALM [12], ORQA [24], Izacard attention-distillation [17], Stochastic RAG [54]; LLaMA-Factory [58]. Motivation cites Cuconasu et al. 2024 "power of noise" [6] for relevance not equalling answer usefulness. Related: authors' follow-up MAO-ARAG [5].

CODE
Algorithm 1 pseudocode (App C, p.18): per question run QR -> Retriever (K docs) -> Selector -> Generator; compute penalties; Rshared = F1 of Ans_predict; store tuple ((O_QR,subq,R_QR),(O_S,IDs,R_S),(O_G,Ans,R_G)) in buffer M; then GAE advantages, loss L(θ,ϕ)=L_Actor+α·L_Critic, update, clear M.
Final reward (Eq 15): 0 for t<T; at t=T, Rshared + P_i − β·log(πθ(Answer_i|O_i)/πθSFT(Answer_i|O_i)).
Prompts for rewriter, selector, generator are in Tables 3-5 (pp.15-17); the generator asks for answers in the form **answer**; the selector outputs e.g. "Document0,Document4,Document6,Document7".

FIGURES
- Fig 1 (p.3): overall framework, with rewriter, frozen retriever, selector, generator, shared F1 reward plus per-agent penalty. Best single picture of the pipeline.
- Fig 2 (p.8): bar ablation removing each agent from joint training, per dataset.
- Fig 3 (p.8): AmbigQA training reward curves vs number of training samples; shows convergence speed.
- Fig 4 (p.17): heuristic for selector SFT labels (word overlap).
I did not run the figures script.

PROBLEMS
No embedded instructions found. Equations garbled in extraction (Eq 11-16 symbols) but legible. Table 7 has values fused with markers (e.g. "50.62" underline artifacts). Reference list has a duplicated PTDE entry [3]/[4]. The reference numbering for Contriever/BGE/E5 in the Table 7 caption ([46],[48]) differs from the main text ([48],[46]), so do not rely on it for attribution.
